messages.subject: understanding WETMASS and Body_cond at debout.
messages.subject_clean: understanding WETMASS and Body_cond at debout.
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

I am trying to run a model of a frog and thus would like to know how its wet mass and body condition vary along time.
However, I could not understand why the starting WETMASS variable does not correspond to the "amass" parameter I included in the function ecto. While I supplied the model with a body mass of 10g, I got values that start at 1.25 that grow along the year. I know the DEB vignette is underway, but thought this might have a quick/simple response.

Thanks to Mike and all for the great job herein!

My parameters are:
                    micro=
                    micro_global(loc = c(-77.104,38.75),
                    timeinterval=365,
                    nyears=1,
                    soiltype=2,
                   REFL= 0.1,
                    slope= 0,
                    aspect= 30,
                    DEP=c(0,2,5,10,15,30,60,90,100,120),
                    minshade= 10,
                    maxshade= 100,
                    RUF = 0.004,
                    PCTWET = 100,
                    CMH2O = 1,
                    runmoist=1
)
 ecto=
ectotherm(
    DEB=1,
   amass= 10#
  ,lometry= 4#
  ,VTMAX =29#
  ,TPREF= 25#
  ,ctmax=40 #
  ,mindepth    = 1 #
  ,maxdepth    = 3 #
  ,skinwet    = 100 #
  ,extref= 20#
)

Then, I get:

w=as.data.frame(ecto$debout[,c(1:5,19)])
with(w, plot(WETMASS~DAY, ylab="wet mass, g", xlab="year",type = "l", main = "wet mass through time"))
with(w, plot((Body_cond)~DAY,ylab="body condition", xlab="year",type = "l", main = "percentage of original body weigth through time"))

Cheers,
Agus

messages.subject: Re: understanding WETMASS and Body_cond at debout.
messages.subject_clean: understanding WETMASS and Body_cond at debout.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Agus,

The reason is that, with the DEB model on, the mass input is overridden and it starts with the initial conditions specified for the DEB model, which have been set by default to that of the lizard Eulamprus quoyii as a fertilised egg. The body condition output (renamed in the soon to be released official first version as the more accurate PCT_DESIC) is zero because you have the parameter 'raindrink' set to zero by default - this parameter is the number of mm of rainfall that must fall before the animal can drink water.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: NicheMapR now can compile locally
messages.body_plain:
Dear NicheMapR users,

After a lot of blind alleys, I've finally figured out how to include the Fortran code of the NicheMapR package so that it compiles locally when installed from source. Thus if you were having trouble installing it on your particular system with the pre-compiled binaries that I was providing, you might now be able to get it to install properly.

Note that to do this on a Windows machine you will also need to have Rtools installed, which can be found at https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/

To install on a mac you will need to make sure you have a Fortran compiler installed. If you run the following two lines in the terminal, it should work:

curl -O http://r.research.att.com/libs/gfortran-4.8.2-darwin13.tar.bz2
sudo tar fvxj gfortran-4.8.2-darwin13.tar.bz2 -C /

I'll provide further details a bit later when I do the next release, but I thought I'd just point this out now.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Modeling Anurans
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I apologize as these are likely basic questions but I am hoping to get confirmation before I dive further into these projects. I have been using NicheMapR to model lizards recently but plan to focus more on amphibians, eventually salamanders, but currently anurans.  I know Niche Mapper was used for the Kearney et al. 2008 Ecography paper which focused on Cane Toads.  However, there are parts of the manuscript where I am unsure if the methods used are also available in NicheMapR.

1) In the methods, there is a mention of cutaneous and respiratory water loss when toads are above ground.  Is there a way to incorporate water loss in NicheMapR?  Or is this a byproduct of other calculations resulting in an estimate based on other parameters?

2)  When modeling eggs and larvae, pond conditions were modeled, which I see in NicheMapR.  However, I don't see parameters for modeling how this impacts egg development (likely me just not knowing the appropriate name of the variables)?  Or were these calculations done using the output of the pond models outside of Niche Mapper/NicheMapR?  Is there

3) More of a request, if there is anyone who has worked with NicheMapR and anurans I would love to chat about it.

Vinny

messages.subject: Re: Modeling Anurans
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

You can set it up to model an anuran (or any other wet-skinned animal) by setting the skin wetness parameter 'pct_wet=100'. That will result in an appropriate cutaneous water loss and associated body temperature effect. You can also choose a frog morphology by setting 'shape=4', or just set it up as an ellipse of appropriate dimensions.

I did the pond calculations by setting up the ectotherm model as a container that fills and empties with rainfall. I happen to be working on an update to that just now. I'll provide a vignette on how to use it soon. It's also possible to use the microclimate model to simulate a pond (making the substrate clay, adding a multiplier to the rainfall and setting the parameter 'maxpool' to be the max depth of the pond). There will be some work coming out on this soon.

Note that up until now the ectotherm model available in NicheMapR is really a beta version lacking full documentation. But I've almost finished all of this and will put a formal release out in the next month as well as submitting a software note for publication.

Urtzi Urzelai, Reid Tingley and I have been working on frogs with NicheMapR quite a bit and there'll be a paper coming out in Ecosphere led by Megan Fitzpatrick on freeze/thaw in frogs soon.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Modeling Anurans
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

I have modelled an anuran species (Rana temporaria) with the help of Reid Tingley and Mike. As Mike said, you can model a frog by setting 'pct_wet = 100', and 'shape = 4' (i.e. shape parameters of Lithobates pipiens). You can always manually change those parameters to match the shape of e.g. salamanders.

Then, I used thermal biology data (locomotor performance curves, thermal gradient experiments, and field observations in some cases) to feed relevant parameters that control activity windows to a large extent. These are T_F_min (minimum foraging temperature), T_F_max (maximum foraging temp), T_B_min (maximum basking temp), T_RB_min (minimum temp to go from retreat to basking site), CT_max, CT_min and T_pref. I used the same value for T_F_min, T_B_min, and T_RB_min. That way I simulated a frog that emerged at a given temperature and started foraging immediatelly, because R. temporaria does not thermoregulate through basking. You might also be interested in checking other 'behavioral' parameters (e.g. is your species noctural? crepuscular? how deep are typical retreats? does activity depend on rainfall?). If you have skin resistance to ewl data, I guess that you could also include that by adjusting pct_wet.

I hope this helps. At any rate, if you want to discuss something I am always opened for that.

Good luck with your project!

Cheers,
Urtzi

messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent!

Regarding metabolic rate, I used the default parameter values of NicheMapR. If you have measured metabolic rates for your species, I would definately use them. However, since ectotherms do not produce (much) heat through metabolism, predictions should not differ that much. But you can always test that! :)

I will be doing field work from 25th of this month to 15th may, and I will have very limited access to internet. Thus, if you want to chat through Skype, we can do that when I am back from the field. Alternatively, if you want to ask me anything by email, you can either post here or email me directly to urtzi.e...@gmail.com whenever you want: I will get back to you as soon as I can (or as soon as I have internet connection).

All the best!
Urtzi

messages.subject: opendap connectivity for micro_aust and micro_usa now works for PC
messages.subject_clean: opendap connectivity for micro_aust and micro_usa now works for PC
messages.body_plain:
Dear NicheMapR users,

I just discovered the RnetCDF package which, unlike ncdf4, allows opendap connectivity on PC (the latter only allowed opendap for OSX and linux). So I've now updated the micro_usa and micro_aust functions to use RnetCDF to connect to the gridMET and AWAP data sets, respectively. I'm very pleased about this!

All the best,
Mike
